decision: I approved the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps'
reason: Approved with --yes

decision: I chose Node.js with Express and Mongoose (mongoose@7) for the sample app.
reason: Node.js is specified by the prompt; Express + Mongoose is a familiar stack for MongoDB-style samples and matches developer expectations.
evidence: Assumption in prompt review: 'Implement as a normal single-process Node.js sample' and readiness report: 'Node.js 24, npx, npm available.'

decision: I chose Mongoose (mongoose@7) as the MongoDB ODM/driver layer.
reason: Mongoose simplifies schema definitions, indexing, and versioned document modeling for a small sample app.
evidence: Assumption: 'Use a current Mongoose 7.x release compatible with Node 24 (e.g., "mongoose@7").'

decision: I chose to read the DocumentDB connection string from the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime.
reason: Keeps secrets out of source and follows the prompt's explicit instruction.
evidence: Skill_md: 'Its connection string is in the environment variable `DOCUMENTDB_URI`. Read it from the environment at run time.'

decision: I chose OpenAI (api.openai.com) as the default LLM provider with model 'gpt-4o-mini' configurable via env.
reason: OpenAI is commonly available and easy to configure; making provider and model configurable avoids locking users in and allows offline testing with a fallback classifier.
evidence: Readiness report: 'LLM provider/model must be chosen and exposed in .env.example; suggested models include gpt-4o-mini.'

decision: I chose a single collection 'collateral_assets' where each valuation update is a new document version (same assetId, incrementing version, createdAt timestamp).
alternatives: Separate collections for assets and valuations
reason: This matches the prompt's versioned-document requirement and simplifies fetching the latest version via aggregation.
evidence: Assumption in prompt review: 'Create one collection (e.g. `collateral_assets`) ... updates insert a new document with same assetId and higher version.'

decision: I chose compound index on assetId+version and a single-field index on createdAt.
alternatives: Compound index on assetId+version and createdAt index
reason: Compound supports fast latest-version queries; createdAt supports time filters.
evidence: documentdb-indexing skill guidance recommending compound ESR indexes and the prompt review suggestion to use {assetId:1,version:-1}.

decision: I chose coverage ratio = sum(latest collateral valuations for eligible assets) / sum(latest liabilities for those assets).
alternatives: Compute coverage as sum(latest valuations) / sum(liabilities)
Compute coverage as asset-level ratio averaged
reason: This formula is straightforward, commonly used in collateralisation contexts, and allows the sample to demonstrate aggregation over latest versions; eligibility is determined by LLM-assigned eligibilityTier (exclude 'ineligible').
evidence: Readiness report flagged 'Coverage ratio formula' as an information gap and asked builder to choose and document.

decision: I chose to make embeddings optional and not create a vector index in the sample; embedding dimension configurable in .env.example if users want to enable it.
alternatives: Create a vector index and store embeddings
Do not create vector index and make embeddings optional
reason: Vector indexes require matching embedding dimensions and cluster support; keeping this optional keeps sample small and safe while still documenting how to enable it.
evidence: Information gap in readiness report about embedding dimension and vector usage; vector search skill advises making dims configurable.

decision: I approved the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps'
reason: Approved with --yes

decision: I chose Node.js with Express and Mongoose (mongoose@7)

evidence: Assumption from prompt review: 'Use a current Mongoose 7.x release compatible with Node 24' and sample asks for 'build a Node.js Mongoose collateral management service'

decision: I chose OpenAI API (OPENAI_API_KEY) as default provider with MODEL_NAME configurable (e.g., gpt-4o-mini or gpt-4o-mini-classification). The sample allows DISABLE_LLM=true to skip classification in environments without keys.
alternatives: Use no LLM and hard-code tags
reason: OpenAI is widely available, the openai npm package is easy to use for a simple classification call, and making it configurable keeps sample flexible.
evidence: Assumption from prompt review: 'Call an LLM via a provider configured in env vars (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY). Default to a lightweight classification model (e.g., an OpenAI classification-capable model...)'

decision: I chose to read the DocumentDB connection string from the DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable at runtime and never write it into repository files.
alternatives: Read DB credentials from a config file
reason: This follows the run environment guidance and security best-practice to avoid committing secrets.
evidence: Skill_md: 'Its connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time. Never write its value into any file...'

decision: I chose not to provision any Azure resources and to use the pre-provisioned cluster referenced by DOCUMENTDB_URI.
alternatives: Do not provision resources (use existing cluster)
reason: Policy forbids creating resources; the cluster already exists and should be used for verification.
evidence: Run policy: 'Azure resource changes allowed: False.' and skill_md: 'a cluster is already provisioned and reachable'

decision: I chose one collection 'collateral_assets' in database 'sample_banking_06' where each version is a new document sharing assetId and having a version integer and createdAt timestamp.
alternatives: One collection with each version as new document (version field)
reason: This matches the prompt requirement and keeps schema simple for sample; it enables efficient time-travel queries via aggregation to pick latest version.
evidence: Assumption from prompt review: 'Each collateral asset and valuation update as a versioned document in DocumentDB (using a version field and createdAt timestamp). Create one collection (e.g. collateral_assets) ... Updates insert a new document with same assetId and higher version.'

decision: I chose the coverage formula: coverage_ratio = sum(latest valuations of assets (optionally only eligible ones)) / totalLiabilities where totalLiabilities is provided by the client as a query parameter. The endpoint will return both numerator and denominator.
alternatives: Compute coverage as sum(latest valuations) / totalLiabilities provided by client
Compute coverage as per-asset liability fields
Compute coverage using external liability collection
reason: Simple, transparent, and easy for a sample to demonstrate aggregation logic; keeps liabilities external so sample stays focused on collateral management.
evidence: readiness_report: 'Coverage ratio formula missing; builder must choose and document.'

decision: I chose to make embeddings optional and configurable; the schema includes an optional embedding field, but the sample will not generate embeddings by default. If provided, embeddings dimension and vector-index instructions are in README and .env.example.
alternatives: Create a vector index and store embeddings
Do not include vector embeddings in sample
reason: Vector search is out of scope for core collateral/coverage demo; keep optional to avoid embedding model dependency and to comply with minimal sample complexity.
evidence: readiness_report: 'If you include vector search... make embedding dimension configurable'

decision: I chose mongodb-memory-server for unit tests (offline in-memory MongoDB) to allow tests to run without network dependencies; tests set DISABLE_LLM=true to avoid external LLM calls.
reason: mongodb-memory-server provides a realistic MongoDB server for integration-style tests without requiring the live cluster and keeps CI-friendly behavior.
evidence: Assumption from prompt review: 'Include basic unit tests using mocking for the DB and LLM so tests can run offline (e.g., jest with mongodb-memory-server or sinon stubs).','readiness_report' guidance

decision: I chose to replace tests to use jest mocks of the Mongoose model instead of mongodb-memory-server after mongodb-memory-server failed to start (spawn Unknown system error -86).

decision: I chose to run the seed script against the live cluster using DOCUMENTDB_URI from the environment to create collections and sample documents for verification.
